definitions.explanation: In modern Japanese, mostly used by people from Hokkaido or Okinawa to refer to the main island of Honshu (and sometimes Honshu plus Shikoku and Kyushu). Roughly "the rest of Japan" from the speaker's perspective.

definitions.gloss: the interior of a country; inland area
definitions.explanation: An inland part of a country, away from the coast or frontier. Less common; appears in some formal or older texts.

examples.japanese: {内地|ないち}から{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{来|き}た。
{沖縄|おきなわ}の{人|ひと}は{本州|ほんしゅう}を{内地|ないち}と{呼|よ}ぶ。
examples.english: People in Okinawa call Honshu the mainland.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{内地|ないち}に{帰省|きせい}する{道民|どうみん}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many Hokkaido residents return to the mainland for the winter holidays.

examples.japanese: この{国|くに}の{内地|ないち}は{乾燥|かんそう}した{気候|きこう}だ。
examples.english: The interior of this country has a dry climate.

examples.japanese: {港湾|こうわん}{都市|とし}と{内地|ないち}を{結|むす}ぶ{鉄道|てつどう}が{整備|せいび}された。
examples.english: A railway connecting the port cities to the interior was developed.

examples.japanese: {沿岸部|えんがんぶ}と{比|くら}べて、{内地|ないち}は{気温差|きおんさ}が{激|はげ}しい。
examples.english: Compared to the coastal areas, the interior has a sharp temperature range.

notes:
Compound of {内|ない} (inner) + {地|ち} (land). In pre-war usage, also meant "Japan proper" as opposed to colonial territories — that usage is now historical and avoided.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内地|ないち}から{来|く}る: to come from the mainland
- {内地|ないち}に{帰|かえ}る: to return to the mainland
- {内地|ないち}{勤務|きんむ}: assignment on the mainland
- {内地|ないち}{留学|りゅうがく}: study at a mainland school (Hokkaido/Okinawa usage)

USAGE:
The "mainland" sense is most natural from a Hokkaido or Okinawa perspective. Honshu speakers rarely call their own islands {内地|ないち}; for them it just sounds like the speaker is from somewhere else.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {本土|ほんど}: the mainland — neutral, can be used by anyone
- {本州|ほんしゅう}: Honshu — the specific main island
- {外地|がいち}: outer territories — historical pair of {内地|ないち}
